At one dealership, most visitors are young riders, many asking about the “championship-winning” models.
Staff say foot traffic has picked up noticeably. The 820RR and 500RR — both linked to race success — are now the biggest draws.
Why the buzz?
Small-displacement four-cylinder engines, strong value for money, and standout track performance against global brands.
Sales aren’t spiking overnight — but they’re steadily climbing.
More importantly, interest is converting: some test riders are placing orders directly via mini-programs.
For buyers, it comes down to three things: price, specs, and delivery time.

ns2:group.ns2:title: Memory prices are plunging at Huaqiangbei, Shenzhen
ns2:group.ns2:description:
At Huaqiangbei — the world’s largest electronics trading hub — memory prices are plunging.
Jiemian News found some units dropped by as much as 2,000 yuan each. One trader said losses “wiped out a house’s worth of gains” — millions of yuan in Shenzhen terms.
“We heard the market was about to crash — profits could vanish within a month,” a store owner said. “So we sold fast. One seller moved 50,000 64GB sticks through WeChat groups.”
The earlier price surge, he added, was driven by hoarding. Demand was weak, inventories were high, and after Chinese New Year, factories restarted and a new wave of supply hit the market.
“If you don’t sell now, you’re stuck.”

ns2:group.ns2:description:
Maison Margiela unveiled its Fall/Winter 2026 collection in Shanghai at the close of Shanghai Fashion Week, marking the house's first-ever runway show in China.
Renzo Rosso, founder of OTB Group, attended in person and said the show reflected an unprecedented fusion between Margiela and the Chinese market.
Set against the atmosphere of a nighttime flea market, the collection reworked broken porcelain, old tapestries, and antique dresses into new forms on the body. The event also opened the Maison Margiela/folders project, which will continue over the next 12 days across Shanghai, Beijing, Chengdu, and Shenzhen through a series of exhibitions and immersive experiences.

ns2:group.ns2:title: Have you heard of aphantasia? Here’s what it is — and how to know if you have it #TEDTalks
ns2:group.ns2:description: Picture this: a rocket ship crash-lands on a planet, and an alien approaches the spacecraft. What do you see in your mind when you visualize this scene? For Alex Rosenthal (and many others), the answer is: absolutely nothing. Exploring the fascinating science of aphantasia, or the inability to generate mental images, he shows why our minds are much more different than we think.
